correctness.rationale: For the specified Fourier convention, applying Q(i∂/(2π)) to the Gaussian gives Q−ΔQ/(4π)+Δ²Q/(32π²); applying a homogeneous quadratic R similarly gives −R+ΔR/(4π). Hence the quadratic term forced by self-duality is −ΔQ/(8π), with exact cancellation of the constant terms; the only free constant is zero at the origin. Polar differentiation gives ΔQ(rω)=r²[4(d+2)A+Δ_SA]. Because A>0, the negative radii satisfy 0<r²<h with h=(d+2)/(2π)+Δ_SA/(8πA), giving exactly v_d E[(h_+)^(d/2)]. The polynomial zero set is null. Integration by parts on the sphere gives E[Δ_SA/A]=E[|∇_S log A|²]; Jensen for the positive-part power proves the bound. The angular term vanishes only for constant A, establishing the sharp radial minimum; in d=2 h_+=h+(-h)_+ gives the additional exact clipping term without assuming h≥0. The inequality is not an equality formula at every nonradial profile in higher dimension.
